name: Computer Science
description: Programming, data structures, algorithms, discrete mathematics, operating systems, networks, databases and software engineering for a first-year undergraduate Computer Science programme.

topics.name: Programming Fundamentals
topics.summary: Type systems, control flow, procedural abstraction and object orientation — the vocabulary every later module assumes.

subtopics.name: Data Types and Variables
subtopics.summary: Primitive and composite types, static versus dynamic typing, and the machine representation of values.

objectives.text: Distinguish primitive from composite data types and state the operations each supports
Explain static versus dynamic typing and strong versus weak typing
Reason about the finite range of fixed-width integer and floating-point representations
Distinguish value semantics from reference semantics during assignment

subtopics.name: Control Flow
subtopics.summary: Selection, iteration and short-circuit evaluation, and how loop structure determines running time.

objectives.text: Trace the execution of nested selection and iteration constructs
Choose between definite and indefinite iteration for a given problem
State and use a loop invariant to argue that a loop is correct
Count the elementary operations a nested loop performs

subtopics.name: Functions, Scope and Parameter Passing
subtopics.summary: Procedural abstraction, lexical scope, the call stack, and the difference between pass-by-value and pass-by-reference.

objectives.text: Explain procedural abstraction and the role of a function contract
Resolve identifiers under lexical scoping rules
Describe how the call stack stores activation records
Contrast pass-by-value, pass-by-reference and pass-by-object-reference

subtopics.name: Object Orientation
subtopics.summary: Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism and dynamic dispatch, and when composition is preferable to inheritance.

objectives.text: Define encapsulation and justify information hiding
Distinguish inheritance from composition and choose between them
Explain subtype polymorphism and dynamic dispatch
Separate an abstract interface from its concrete implementations

topics.name: Data Structures
topics.summary: Abstract data types and their concrete representations, with the asymptotic cost of every core operation.

subtopics.name: Arrays and Dynamic Arrays
subtopics.summary: Contiguous storage, address arithmetic, and the amortised analysis of a doubling dynamic array.

objectives.text: Compute the address of an array element from base address and index
State the asymptotic cost of access, search, insertion and deletion on an array
Explain why a doubling dynamic array gives amortised constant-time append
Choose between a static and a dynamic array for a given workload

subtopics.name: Linked Lists
subtopics.summary: Singly, doubly and circular lists, pointer manipulation, and the trade-off against contiguous storage.

objectives.text: Describe the node structure of singly, doubly and circular linked lists
Write the pointer updates for insertion and deletion at a known node
State the asymptotic cost of each linked list operation
Compare linked lists with dynamic arrays on locality and memory overhead

subtopics.name: Stacks and Queues
subtopics.summary: LIFO and FIFO abstract data types, circular buffer implementation, and their canonical applications.

objectives.text: State the LIFO and FIFO disciplines and the interface of each ADT
Implement a queue as a circular buffer over a fixed array
Apply a stack to expression evaluation and delimiter matching
Select a stack or a queue given the required traversal order

subtopics.name: Binary Search Trees
subtopics.summary: Tree terminology, the BST ordering invariant, traversals, and why balance governs performance.

objectives.text: Define root, height, depth, internal node and leaf for a rooted tree
State the binary search tree ordering invariant and verify it for a given tree
Produce pre-order, in-order and post-order traversals of a binary tree
Explain why BST operations cost the height and how balancing bounds it

subtopics.name: Hash Tables
subtopics.summary: Hash functions, load factor, separate chaining and open addressing, and expected constant-time lookup.

objectives.text: Explain how a hash function maps keys to bucket indices
Define load factor and relate it to expected probe length
Compare separate chaining with open addressing as collision strategies
State the average and worst-case costs of hash table operations

topics.name: Algorithms
topics.summary: Asymptotic analysis, searching, sorting and recursive divide-and-conquer design.

subtopics.name: Asymptotic Complexity Analysis
subtopics.summary: Formal definitions of big-O, big-Omega and big-Theta, growth-rate ordering, and how to analyse loops.

objectives.text: State the formal definition of big-O, big-Omega and big-Theta
Order the standard complexity classes by asymptotic growth
Derive the running time of nested and halving loops
Distinguish best-case, worst-case and average-case analysis from asymptotic bounds

subtopics.name: Searching Algorithms
subtopics.summary: Linear search, binary search, the sortedness precondition, and the comparison-based lower bound.

objectives.text: Trace linear search and state its best and worst-case cost
Trace binary search on a sorted array and count the comparisons
Justify the logarithmic bound on binary search from the halving recurrence
Decide when sorting first to enable binary search is worthwhile

subtopics.name: Sorting Algorithms
subtopics.summary: Insertion, selection, merge and quicksort, with stability, in-place behaviour and the comparison lower bound.

objectives.text: Trace insertion sort and selection sort on a small array
Explain merge sort and derive its running time from its recurrence
Explain quicksort partitioning and identify its worst case
Compare sorting algorithms on time, space and stability

subtopics.name: Recursion and Divide and Conquer
subtopics.summary: Base cases, recursive structure, recurrence relations, the master theorem and memoisation.

objectives.text: Identify the base case and recursive case of a recursive definition
Write a recurrence relation for a recursive algorithm
Apply the master theorem to solve a divide-and-conquer recurrence
Explain how memoisation removes redundant recursive work

topics.name: Discrete Mathematics for Computing
topics.summary: The mathematical language of computing: sets, relations, propositional logic, graphs and counting.

subtopics.name: Sets, Relations and Functions
subtopics.summary: Set operations, cardinality, Cartesian products, relation properties and classes of function.

objectives.text: Perform union, intersection, difference and complement on finite sets
Compute the cardinality of a power set and a Cartesian product
Test a relation for reflexivity, symmetry, antisymmetry and transitivity
Classify a function as injective, surjective or bijective

subtopics.name: Propositional Logic
subtopics.summary: Connectives, truth tables, logical equivalence, De Morgan's laws and valid inference rules.

objectives.text: Construct the truth table of a compound proposition
Identify tautologies, contradictions and logically equivalent formulae
Apply De Morgan's laws and the contrapositive correctly
Distinguish valid inference rules from common logical fallacies

subtopics.name: Graph Theory
subtopics.summary: Graph terminology, degree sum, representations, traversal and shortest-path reasoning.

objectives.text: Define vertex, edge, degree, path, cycle and connectedness
Apply the handshaking lemma relating degree sum to edge count
Compare adjacency matrix and adjacency list representations
Trace breadth-first and depth-first traversal of a small graph

subtopics.name: Combinatorics
subtopics.summary: Product and sum rules, permutations, combinations, inclusion-exclusion and the pigeonhole principle.

objectives.text: Apply the product rule and the sum rule to counting problems
Distinguish permutations from combinations and compute each
Use the inclusion-exclusion principle on overlapping sets
Apply the pigeonhole principle to prove an existence claim

topics.name: Databases
topics.summary: The relational model, functional dependency and normalisation, and SQL as a declarative query language.

subtopics.name: The Relational Model
subtopics.summary: Relations, attributes, tuples, keys, integrity constraints and the core relational algebra operators.

objectives.text: Define relation, attribute, tuple, degree and cardinality
Identify candidate, primary and foreign keys in a schema
State the entity integrity and referential integrity rules
Apply selection, projection and join from relational algebra

subtopics.name: Normalisation
subtopics.summary: Functional dependencies, the anomalies redundancy causes, and decomposition to 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and BCNF.

objectives.text: Define a functional dependency and read one from a schema
Describe insertion, update and deletion anomalies caused by redundancy
Test a relation against 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and BCNF
Decompose an unnormalised relation losslessly into third normal form

subtopics.name: SQL Fundamentals
subtopics.summary: SELECT structure, filtering, joins, aggregation with GROUP BY and HAVING, and NULL semantics.

objectives.text: Write a SELECT statement with projection, filtering and ordering
Join two or more tables and distinguish inner from outer joins
Aggregate rows with GROUP BY and filter groups with HAVING
Predict the result of comparisons and aggregates involving NULL

topics.name: Computer Systems
topics.summary: How software shares a machine, and how machines share a network.

subtopics.name: Operating Systems
subtopics.summary: Processes, scheduling, memory and the job of an OS.

objectives.text: State the functions of an operating system
Distinguish a process from a thread and explain ready/running/waiting
Explain why CPU scheduling and virtual memory exist

subtopics.name: Computer Networks
subtopics.summary: Layered models, IP addressing and reliable delivery.

objectives.text: Compare the OSI and TCP/IP models
Explain IP addresses, ports and the difference between TCP and UDP
Describe a simple request/response on the web

topics.name: Software Engineering
topics.summary: How non-trivial software is planned, built and checked.

subtopics.name: Software Process
subtopics.summary: Lifecycle models and why process exists on a team project.

objectives.text: Describe waterfall, iterative and agile process models
State typical activities: requirements, design, implementation, testing, maintenance
Choose a model for a given project constraint

subtopics.name: Testing and Debugging
subtopics.summary: Unit, integration and system tests, and a disciplined way to find faults.

objectives.text: Distinguish faults, failures and errors
Write a small unit-test example and explain coverage
Outline a systematic debugging procedure
